questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of flow control in TCP?

options.text: To prevent the sender from overwhelming the receiver.
To prevent congestion in the network.
To increase the speed of data transmission.

questions.explanation: Flow control is designed to match the data transmission rate of the sender with the receiver's ability to process data, preventing buffer overflow at the receiver.

questions.stem: During which TCP congestion control phase does the congestion window grow exponentially?
questions.explanation: In the slow start phase, the congestion window size increases exponentially with each acknowledgment received, doubling every round-trip time until the slow start threshold is reached.

questions.stem: If a TCP connection has a slow start threshold (ssthresh) of 10 MSS and the current congestion window (cwnd) is 5 MSS, what will the cwnd be after 2 RTTs assuming no packet loss? Provide your answer in MSS.
questions.explanation: The connection is in the slow start phase since cwnd < ssthresh. The cwnd doubles every RTT. Starting from 5 MSS, after 1 RTT, cwnd = 10 MSS, and after 2 RTTs, cwnd = 20 MSS.

questions.stem: How does TCP infer network congestion?

options.text: By measuring the time taken for acknowledgments to return.
By counting the number of packets sent.
By monitoring the receiver's buffer size.

questions.explanation: TCP infers congestion primarily through packet loss, which is detected by the absence of acknowledgments or the receipt of duplicate acknowledgments.

questions.stem: What happens to the congestion window when TCP detects packet loss?

options.text: It is reduced to half of its current size.

questions.explanation: When TCP detects packet loss, it interprets this as a sign of congestion and reduces the congestion window to half of its current size to alleviate congestion.

questions.stem: A TCP connection experiences packet loss when the congestion window is 16 MSS. What will the new congestion window be after the loss is detected? Provide your answer in MSS.
questions.explanation: Upon detecting packet loss, TCP reduces the congestion window to half of its current size. Therefore, if the window was 16 MSS, it will be reduced to 8 MSS.

questions.stem: Explain the purpose of the slow start threshold (ssthresh) in TCP congestion control.
markingGuide: Defines the boundary between slow start and congestion avoidance.
When cwnd reaches ssthresh, TCP transitions from exponential to linear growth.
Helps prevent network congestion by controlling the growth rate of cwnd.
questions.explanation: The slow start threshold (ssthresh) is a critical parameter in TCP congestion control. It defines the point at which TCP transitions from the slow start phase, with exponential growth, to the congestion avoidance phase, with linear growth. This transition helps manage the rate of data flow and prevents congestion by avoiding excessive data injection into the network.

questions.stem: In which phase does TCP increase the congestion window size by 1 MSS per RTT?
questions.explanation: During the congestion avoidance phase, TCP increases the congestion window size linearly, by 1 MSS per round-trip time, to carefully manage network resources and prevent congestion.

questions.stem: Discuss how TCP's congestion control algorithms contribute to network fairness.
markingGuide: TCP congestion control aims to share network resources fairly among connections.
Slow start and congestion avoidance adjust sending rates based on network conditions.
Packet loss detection and window size reduction prevent any single connection from dominating bandwidth.
questions.explanation: TCP's congestion control algorithms are designed to ensure fairness in network resource usage. By adjusting the sending rate based on network conditions through slow start and congestion avoidance, TCP prevents any single connection from monopolizing bandwidth. Additionally, the detection of packet loss and subsequent reduction of the congestion window size help maintain a balance, allowing multiple connections to coexist and share the network fairly.
